catalog: AI Governance Layer — what the delivered replica does today
about: Answers to client product questions ('is this active?', 'can we already do this?') come only from this file (PD-51). It is maintained in the repository and reviewed like code; 'active' means the listed checks of the scenario suite prove it, and the gateway adds the result of the latest verification run. It is never read from production.

statuses.active: works today and is proven by the listed checks
statuses.partial: works, with the limit stated in the note
statuses.out_of_scope: not part of the replica; decided for the client's own environment

features.name: Only EU-resident models
features.what: A model endpoint outside the EU cannot be registered, approved, enabled by exception or reached over the network.

features.name: CONFIDENTIAL work stays on the self-hosted model
features.what: Requests classified CONFIDENTIAL are answered only by the model running on the company's own server.

features.name: RESTRICTED data never goes to any model
features.what: Production data, secrets and special-category personal data are refused before any model is called.

features.name: Credentials and keys in prompts are blocked
features.what: API keys, tokens, private keys and connection strings stop the request; only the type of finding is recorded.

features.name: Personal data in prompts is blocked
features.what: Email addresses, phone numbers and IBANs stop the request instead of being masked. Allowed: the caller's own registered address, and addresses on domains reserved for tests (example.com, *.test).

features.name: Prompts, answers and agent commands are stored
features.what: Every request that reaches a model is stored with its answer, encrypted per team, for 30 days; so is every command an agent asks to run, with its output. Reading one takes two people: security or the DPO asks with a reason, a different person approves, and the read is logged with both names. The DPO can erase them per person or per request.

features.name: Client product questions
features.what: People on the client side (in the PoC a demo persona: there is no client yet) ask what the platform can do and get answers from this catalog. They cannot send free prompts, code or repository context.

features.name: No governance, no tool
features.what: If the policy engine, the audit store, the content store or the model is unavailable, requests stop; nothing falls back to an ungoverned path.

features.name: Hard budget caps per team and organisation
features.what: Requests stop at 100 % of the envelope; a warning is returned from 80 %.

features.name: Budget top-ups need a second person
features.what: A top-up is requested by one person and approved by another; self-approval is refused.

features.name: Tamper-evident audit record
features.what: Every decision is written once to a hash-chained, append-only store with write-once (Object Lock) copies and daily anchors; edits and deletions are refused or detected.

features.name: Repositories are quarantined from AI until cleared
features.what: A repository is closed to AI until its gate items are true and two people sign off; any item turning false closes it again.

features.name: Production data cannot be mounted for agents
features.what: Only synthetic or masked datasets can be attached to an agent sandbox.

features.name: Agent sandboxes
features.what: Ephemeral containers with no credentials and a network that reaches only the gateway; every command is checked by policy before it runs.
features.note: Verified with network probes (PD-46); the scenario suite does not start a sandbox.

features.name: Claude Code routed through the gateway
features.what: Managed settings send Claude Code's requests to the gateway, where all the rules above apply.
features.note: Works from a terminal. Sessions started from the Claude desktop app override the managed settings (PD-38).

features.name: Each verification run records the configuration in force
features.what: A run starts with digests of the policy bundle, egress allowlist, workflow templates, compose file and this catalog, and reports drift from the previous run.

features.name: Sign-in with the company identity provider
features.what: Users sign in through the corporate IdP; the replica uses a built-in development issuer with seeded users.

features.name: Source code hosted and built only in the EU
features.what: Repositories and CI runners move to EU-resident hosting once real code is involved; for the PoC the repository (synthetic code) stays on GitHub.com (owner, 2026-10-21).

features.name: Personal data and secrets checked in commits and pull request text
features.what: The same blocking rules applied to what agents write: diffs, PR descriptions, CI logs.

features.name: A frontier model in an EU cloud region
features.what: A large hosted model (for example Claude in an EU region of a cloud provider) needs the client's cloud account and spend; the replica runs only the self-hosted model.
